key_violations.original: 1. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)). Your firm conducts microbiological analyses of components and drug products for your customers. You perform (b)(4) pour plate methods for microbial enumeration of (b)(4) samples. During the inspection, our investigator observed that your microbiologist failed to record the (b)(4) results when they were assessed as too numerous to count (TNTC), recording only the pour plate counts. The investigator also noted that while the (b)(4) for the pour plate samples was cracked and desiccated, the pour plate counts were recorded as within acceptable limits. When (b)(4) plates are desiccated and cracked, the media can no longer reliably support uniform microbial growth. A result recorded from a compromised plate, even one that falls within specification, cannot be considered valid, as the physical condition of the media may have suppressed or obscured actual microbial recovery. Additionally, your data review procedure is deficient in that it does not require secondary verification when an initial plate count is recorded as 0 colony forming units (CFU), creating a systemic gap where microbial growth can go undetected. During the inspection, the investigator identified a colony on a plate recorded as 0 CFU by your analyst. Further, several samples with desiccated and cracked (b)(4) were recorded as 0 CFU and discarded without secondary analyst review. The practice of non-reporting of TNTC (b)(4) results, and the investigator's direct observation of a colony on a plate recorded as 0 CFU illustrates the unreliability of your data, and further demonstrates that lack of secondary verification is unacceptable.
key_violations.description: 1. 귀사는 실험실 기록에 설정된 규격 및 기준 적합성을 보장하는 데 필요한 모든 시험에서 얻은 완전한 데이터가 포함되도록 보장하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.194(a)). 귀사는 고객사를 위해 원료(components) 및 의약품의 미생물 분석을 수행한다. 귀사는 (b)(4) 시료의 미생물 계수를 위해 (b)(4) 평판 주입법(pour plate)을 수행한다. 실사 중 조사관은 귀사 미생물 담당자가 (b)(4) 결과가 너무 많아 셀 수 없음(TNTC)으로 판정된 경우 그 결과를 기록하지 않고 평판 주입법 계수만 기록한 것을 관찰했다. 조사관은 또한 평판 주입 시료의 (b)(4)가 갈라지고 건조된 상태였음에도 평판 계수가 허용 한도 이내로 기록된 것을 확인했다. (b)(4) 평판이 건조되고 갈라지면 배지는 더 이상 균일한 미생물 성장을 신뢰성 있게 지지할 수 없다. 손상된 평판에서 기록된 결과는 규격 이내라 하더라도 유효한 것으로 볼 수 없는데, 배지의 물리적 상태가 실제 미생물 회수를 억제하거나 가렸을 수 있기 때문이다. 아울러 귀사의 데이터 검토 절차는 초기 평판 계수가 0 집락형성단위(CFU)로 기록된 경우 2차 확인(secondary verification)을 요구하지 않는다는 점에서 결함이 있으며, 이는 미생물 성장이 검출되지 않고 넘어갈 수 있는 시스템적 공백을 만든다. 실사 중 조사관은 귀사 분석자가 0 CFU로 기록한 평판에서 집락 하나를 확인했다. 나아가 (b)(4)가 건조되고 갈라진 여러 시료가 0 CFU로 기록된 뒤 2차 분석자 검토 없이 폐기되었다. TNTC (b)(4) 결과를 보고하지 않는 관행과, 0 CFU로 기록된 평판에서 조사관이 집락을 직접 관찰한 사실은 귀사 데이터의 신뢰성 결여를 보여주며, 2차 확인의 부재가 용인될 수 없음을 추가로 입증한다.
key_violations.risk: 부적합(TNTC) 결과의 선택적 누락과 손상 배지 판독으로 고객사에 발행된 미생물 시험 결과 자체를 신뢰할 수 없게 되어, 오염된 원료·의약품이 적합 판정을 받고 출하될 수 있다.

key_violations.original: 2. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm failed to investigate aberrant media conditions (e.g., cracked or desiccated (b)(4) plates) used for testing raw material and drug product samples in your microbiological laboratory. In your response, you state that you opened an investigation to determine the scope of affected samples and adequacy of results and transferred microbial samples into an alternative incubator as an interim measure. Based on analyst interviews and a limited records review, you concluded that the results are valid. We acknowledge your plan to retest affected samples as a means of confirming your initial test results. Your response is inadequate. Without photographic evidence of plate conditions at the time of reading, there is no basis to retroactively confirm any result. Your conclusions rely solely on analyst interviews and data records that you acknowledged are unreliable. Furthermore, you did not commit to discontinuing the use of damaged plates for microbiological testing.
key_violations.description: 2. 귀사는 배치(batch)가 이미 유통되었는지 여부와 관계없이, 원인 불명의 불일치(discrepancy) 또는 배치나 그 구성성분의 규격 부적합을 철저히 조사하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.192). 귀사는 미생물 실험실에서 원료 및 의약품 시료 시험에 사용된 배지의 이상 상태(예: 갈라지거나 건조된 (b)(4) 평판)를 조사하지 않았다. 귀사는 회신에서 영향받은 시료의 범위와 결과의 적절성을 판단하기 위한 조사를 개시했으며, 임시 조치로 미생물 시료를 대체 배양기로 옮겼다고 밝혔다. 분석자 면담과 제한적인 기록 검토를 근거로 귀사는 결과가 유효하다고 결론지었다. 당국은 초기 시험 결과를 확인하는 수단으로 영향받은 시료를 재시험하겠다는 귀사의 계획을 인지한다. 귀사의 회신은 불충분하다. 판독 시점의 평판 상태에 대한 사진 증거 없이는 어떤 결과도 소급하여 확인할 근거가 없다. 귀사의 결론은 오로지 분석자 면담과, 귀사 스스로 신뢰할 수 없다고 인정한 데이터 기록에만 의존하고 있다. 더욱이 귀사는 손상된 평판을 미생물 시험에 사용하는 것을 중단하겠다고 약속하지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: 배지 이상에 대한 조사 없이 결과를 유효로 결론지어, 손상 배지로 얻은 위음성 결과가 계속 생성·보고될 수 있다.

key_violations.original: 3. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your QU lacked adequate oversight and control over your laboratory operations to ensure a state of control and adherence to applicable quality standards. Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accord with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your laboratory operations, we found your QU is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities.
key_violations.description: 3. 귀사 품질 조직(quality unit, QU)은 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity), 함량(strength), 품질(quality), 순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22). 귀사 QU는 관리 상태(state of control)와 해당 품질 기준의 준수를 보장하기 위한 실험실 운영에 대한 적절한 감독과 통제가 부족했다. 이 서한의 중대한 지적사항들은 귀사가 CGMP에 부합하는 효과적인 품질 시스템을 운영하지 않고 있음을 보여준다. 실험실 운영에 대한 효과적인 경영 감독의 부재에 더하여, 당국은 귀사 QU가 적절한 권한을 행사할 수 있도록 되어 있지 않거나 그 책임을 불충분하게 이행했음을 확인했다.
key_violations.risk: QU의 실험실 감독 부재로 데이터 무결성 결함이 장기간(2025년 2월 이후) 미검출되어, 위탁시험 결과에 의존하는 고객사 전체의 출하 판정이 흔들릴 수 있다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 2026년 6월 22일자 Form FDA 483 회신을 상세히 검토하고 불충분하다고 평가했다. 귀사는 분석자 면담과 실험실 데이터 소급 검토 결과 2025년 2월부터 일관되지 않은 보고 관행이 있었고, 일부 분석자가 (b)(4) 결과가 TNTC(규격 부적합)일 때는 평판 주입법 결과만, 규격 이내일 때만 (b)(4) 결과를 기록하는 등 선택적으로 기록했음을 인정하며 절차 개정·분석자 교육·평판 판독 정기 감사를 약속했다. 그러나 FDA는 이 기간의 TNTC 결과 선택적 누락이 고객사에 발행한 시험성적서(certificates of analysis)의 정확성에 영향을 미쳤는지, 고객사가 불완전하거나 부정확할 수 있는 미생물 데이터를 받았는지를 다루지 않았고, 2차 검토를 요구하도록 보고 절차를 개정했지만 검토한 과거 데이터의 완전성·정확성을 검증할 증거를 제시하지 않았다고 지적했다. 배지 이상 조사에 대해서는 판독 시점 사진 증거가 없어 소급 확인 근거가 없고, 결론이 분석자 면담과 귀사 스스로 신뢰할 수 없다고 인정한 기록에만 의존하며, 손상 평판 사용 중단을 약속하지 않았다고 평가했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일(15 business days) 이내 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov 로 서면 회신
items: 실험실 관행·절차·방법·장비·문서화·분석자 역량에 대한 포괄적 독립 평가를 수행하고, 이를 바탕으로 실험실 시스템 개선 및 유효성 평가를 위한 상세 계획을 제출한다.
제조·실험실 운영 전반의 문서화 시스템을 평가하고, 귀속성·가독성·완전성·원본성·정확성·동시성(attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous) 기록 보존을 보장하는 상세 CAPA 계획을 수립한다.
일탈·불일치·불만·OOS·OOL·실패 조사 시스템 전반의 독립 평가 및 개선 계획과, 자격 있는 컨설턴트가 감독하는 미생물 배지 취급 CAPA(시료 고유 라벨링, 취급자 서명, 시료 무결성·보관 연속성 추적, 활동 일시 기록, 판독 시점 모든 평판의 디지털 타임스탬프 사진 등)를 수립한다.
QU가 효과적으로 기능할 권한과 자원을 갖도록 하는 포괄적 평가·개선 계획을 제출하고, 21 CFR 211.34 에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트를 통해 전체 운영에 대한 6대 시스템(six-system) 감사와 CAPA 완료·유효성 평가를 받는다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 귀사가 시험한 의약품은 section 501(a)(2)(B) 에 따른 불량의약품(adulterated)으로 간주된다. 미해결 위반은 다른 연방기관의 계약 수주를 막을 수 있고, FDA가 수출증명서(Export Certificates) 발급을 보류할 수 있다. 위반이 완전히 해소되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 귀사를 의약품 제조소로 기재한 신규 신청 또는 보완 신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, 시정 조치 완료를 확인하기 위한 재실사가 이루어질 수 있다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 실험실 기록에 설정된 규격 및 기준(specifications and standards) 적합성을 보장하는 데 필요한 모든 시험에서 얻은 완전한 데이터(complete data)가 포함되도록 보장하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
귀사는 배치(batch)가 이미 유통되었는지 여부와 관계없이, 원인 불명의 불일치(unexplained discrepancy) 또는 배치나 그 구성성분의 규격 부적합(failure to meet specifications)을 철저히 조사(thoroughly investigate)하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.192).
귀사 품질 조직(quality unit)은 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity), 함량(strength), 품질(quality), 순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격(established specifications)을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.22).

060af7eeccbf.source_text: during an inspection of your contract testing laboratory, Eurofins SF Analytical Laboratories, Inc., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3014704316, at 215 Witmer Road, Horsham, Pennsylvania, from June 1 to 3, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, the drug products you tested are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). We reviewed your June 22, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)). Your firm conducts microbiological analyses of components and drug products for your customers. You perform (b)(4) pour plate methods for microbial enumeration of (b)(4) samples. During the inspection, our investigator observed that your microbiologist failed to record the (b)(4) results when they were assessed as too numerous to count (TNTC), recording only the pour plate counts. The investigator also noted that while the (b)(4) for the pour plate samples was cracked and desiccated, the pour plate counts were recorded as within acceptable limits. When (b)(4) plates are desiccated and cracked, the media can no longer reliably support uniform microbial growth. A result recorded from a compromised plate, even one that falls within specification, cannot be considered valid, as the physical condition of the media may have suppressed or obscured actual microbial recovery. Additionally, your data review procedure is deficient in that it does not require secondary verification when an initial plate count is recorded as 0 colony forming units (CFU), creating a systemic gap where microbial growth can go undetected. During the inspection, the investigator identified a colony on a plate recorded as 0 CFU by your analyst. Further, several samples with desiccated and cracked (b)(4) were recorded as 0 CFU and discarded without secondary analyst review. The practice of non-reporting of TNTC (b)(4) results, and the investigator's direct observation of a colony on a plate recorded as 0 CFU illustrates the unreliability of your data, and further demonstrates that lack of secondary verification is unacceptable. In your response, you state that analyst interviews and a retrospective review of laboratory data revealed inconsistent reporting practices dating back to February 2025. You acknowledge that some analysts were selectively recording test results, documenting only pour plate results when (b)(4) results were TNTC (out of specification), and only documenting (b)(4) results when they were within specification. You commit to revising your procedures, training analysts, and periodically auditing plate readings. Your response is inadequate. You do not address whether the selective omission TNTC (b)(4) results during this period affected the accuracy of certificates of analysis issued to customers, or whether any customers received incomplete or potentially inaccurate microbiological data. Although you updated your reporting procedure to require secondary review, you provided no evidence to verify the completeness and accuracy of the historical data reviewed. Reliability of data is compromised when there is a failure to maintain complete records of the conditions and data associated with all tests. Furthermore, the lack of complete data compromises the quality unit’s (QU) ability to exercise its function of ensuring compliance to applicable standards. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive independent assessment of your laboratory practices, procedures, methods, equipment, documentation, and analyst competencies. Based on this review, provide a detailed plan to remediate and evaluate the effectiveness of your laboratory system. A comprehensive assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous records throughout your operation. 2. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm failed to investigate aberrant media conditions (e.g., cracked or desiccated (b)(4) plates) used for testing raw material and drug product samples in your microbiological laboratory. In your response, you state that you opened an investigation to determine the scope of affected samples and adequacy of results and transferred microbial samples into an alternative incubator as an interim measure. Based on analyst interviews and a limited records review, you concluded that the results are valid. We acknowledge your plan to retest affected samples as a means of confirming your initial test results. Your response is inadequate. Without photographic evidence of plate conditions at the time of reading, there is no basis to retroactively confirm any result. Your conclusions rely solely on analyst interviews and data records that you acknowledged are unreliable. Furthermore, you did not commit to discontinuing the use of damaged plates for microbiological testing. Data integrity depends on complete and accurate documentation of test results and conditions. Failure to maintain such records undermines the reliability of your data. The use of deficient media similarly compromises the validity of microbiological test results and raises questions about the suitability and robustness of your methods. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, out-of-specification results, out-of-limit results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system. Your action plan should include, but not be limited to, significant improvements in investigation competencies, scope determination, root cause evaluation, CAPA effectiveness, QU oversight, and written procedures. Address how your firm will ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. A comprehensive CAPA plan, overseen by a qualified consultant, for handling microbiological sampling media to ensure robust and reliable data. Establish a system that ensures uninterrupted custody and full reconciliation of all microbiological samples, including but not limited to: o Unique labeling of each sample o Signatures of all staff who handle the sample o Complete tracking of sample integrity and custody o Date and time of each activity (e.g., sample collection, delivery, incubation, removal from incubator) o Digital time-stamped photos of all plates at the time of reading. Ensure full implementation of photographic evidence to support all results obtained. o Signatures of personnel performing reading of microbial counts o Provisions for verifications and routine quality assurance oversight. 3. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your QU lacked adequate oversight and control over your laboratory operations to ensure a state of control and adherence to applicable quality standards. Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accord with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your laboratory operations, we found your QU is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities. Executive management should immediately and comprehensively assess your company’s global manufacturing operations to ensure that your systems, processes, and products conform to FDA requirements. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. See FDA’s guidance documents ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System and Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations for help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211 at https://www.fda.gov/media/71553/download and https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download, respectively. In response to this letter, provide a comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. CGMP Consultant Recommended Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. key_violations.original: 1. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm contract manufactures non-sterile over-the-counter (OTC) (b)(4) drug products, including those labeled for use in (b)(4) . You failed to adequately investigate out-of-specification (OOS) microbiological testing results for components used to manufacture your drug products. For example, in November 2025, you obtained OOS microbiological results for (b)(4) lots (b)(4) . You prepared (b)(4) independent samples from each lot. You tested (b)(4) of the samples for total aerobic microbial count and the (b)(4) samples for total yeast and mold count. One sample from each lot exceeded your total yeast and mold count acceptance criterion of no more than (b)(4) colony forming units per gram. You did not perform an appropriate investigation into the OOS results. Rather, you invalidated the OOS results by averaging the (b)(4) total yeast and mold count sample results to obtain a passing result. You also revised your microbiological sampling plan to allow for averaging of test results for component testing. This practice is not in accordance with the United States Pharmacopeia <61> test method and is unacceptable as it obscures the detection of non-uniform microbiological contamination within a lot. You subsequently released (b)(4) lots and used them in the manufacture of (b)(4) Lot (b)(4) , distributed in (b)(4) .
key_violations.description: 1. 귀사는 배치가 이미 유통되었는지 여부와 관계없이, 원인 불명의 불일치 또는 배치나 그 구성성분의 규격 부적합을 철저히 조사하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.192). 귀사는 (b)(4) 용도로 표시된 제품을 포함한 비무균 일반의약품(OTC) (b)(4) 의약품을 위탁 제조한다. 귀사는 의약품 제조에 사용되는 원료(components)의 규격 외(OOS) 미생물 시험 결과를 적절히 조사하지 않았다. 예를 들어 2025년 11월 귀사는 (b)(4) 로트 (b)(4)에 대해 OOS 미생물 결과를 얻었다. 귀사는 각 로트에서 (b)(4)개의 독립 시료를 조제했다. 귀사는 시료 중 (b)(4)개는 총호기성미생물수(total aerobic microbial count)를, (b)(4)개는 총진균수(total yeast and mold count)를 시험했다. 각 로트에서 시료 1개가 그램당 (b)(4) 집락형성단위 이하라는 총진균수 허용 기준을 초과했다. 귀사는 OOS 결과에 대해 적절한 조사를 수행하지 않았다. 대신 (b)(4)개의 총진균수 시료 결과를 평균하여 적합 결과를 얻는 방식으로 OOS 결과를 무효화했다. 귀사는 또한 원료 시험에서 시험 결과의 평균을 허용하도록 미생물 검체 채취 계획을 개정했다. 이러한 관행은 미국약전(United States Pharmacopeia) <61> 시험법에 부합하지 않으며, 로트 내 불균일한 미생물 오염의 검출을 가리므로 용인될 수 없다. 귀사는 이후 (b)(4) 로트를 출하 승인하여 (b)(4) 로트 (b)(4) 제조에 사용했고, 이 제품은 (b)(4)에 유통되었다.
key_violations.risk: 개별 부적합 결과를 평균으로 무효화해 진균 오염 원료가 출하·사용되었고, 로트 내 불균일 오염이 은폐되어 오염 제품이 시장에 유통될 수 있다.

key_violations.original: Notably, on (b)(4) , your customer, (b)(4) , initiated a Class I recall of (b)(4) lots of (b)(4) manufactured at your facility due to potential fungal contamination in your (b)(4) . The investigation associated with this recall is inadequate. For example, you implemented (b)(4) of incoming (b)(4) prior to filling to reduce bioburden, but subsequent OOS microbiological results obtained from (b)(4) lots demonstrate this corrective action was ineffective. Additionally, your change control associated with the (b)(4) process did not include ensuring appropriate validation of the process as well as evaluation of the (b)(4) . Further, you lacked cleaning procedures for the (b)(4) line, did not conduct cleaning validation of the (b)(4) line, and failed to include yeast and mold microbiological testing as part of your environmental monitoring program. Though your investigation into the potential fungal contamination documented an evaluation of the cleaning procedures and environmental monitoring, it did not identify nor appropriately follow-up on these risks related to potential mold contamination.
key_violations.description: 특히 (b)(4)에 귀사 고객사 (b)(4)는 귀사 (b)(4)의 잠재적 진균 오염을 이유로 귀사 시설에서 제조된 (b)(4)의 (b)(4) 로트에 대해 Class I 회수(recall)를 개시했다. 이 회수와 관련된 조사는 불충분하다. 예를 들어 귀사는 생물부하(bioburden)를 줄이기 위해 충전 전 입고 (b)(4)에 대해 (b)(4)를 시행했으나, 이후 (b)(4) 로트에서 얻어진 OOS 미생물 결과는 이 시정 조치가 효과가 없었음을 보여준다. 아울러 (b)(4) 공정과 관련된 귀사의 변경관리(change control)에는 해당 공정의 적절한 밸리데이션 보장과 (b)(4)에 대한 평가가 포함되지 않았다. 나아가 귀사는 (b)(4) 라인에 대한 세척 절차가 없었고, (b)(4) 라인의 세척 밸리데이션을 수행하지 않았으며, 환경 모니터링 프로그램에 효모·곰팡이(yeast and mold) 미생물 시험을 포함하지 않았다. 잠재적 진균 오염에 대한 귀사의 조사는 세척 절차와 환경 모니터링에 대한 평가를 문서화했으나, 잠재적 곰팡이 오염과 관련된 이러한 리스크를 식별하지도, 적절히 후속 조치하지도 않았다.
key_violations.risk: Class I 회수로 이어진 진균 오염의 근본 원인(세척 절차·세척 밸리데이션·효모/곰팡이 환경 모니터링 부재)이 규명되지 않아 오염 재발 가능성이 높다.

Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). For example, your QU failed to: Validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(2)). key_violations.description: 2. 귀사 품질 조직은 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity), 함량(strength), 품질(quality), 순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22). 귀사 QU는 OTC (b)(4) 의약품 제조 운영을 적절히 감독하지 않았다. 예를 들어 귀사 QU는 다음을 이행하지 않았다: 적절한 주기로 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 밸리데이션 및 신뢰성 확립(21 CFR 211.84(d)(2)). 의약품의 안정성 특성을 평가하도록 설계된 서면 시험 프로그램의 준수(21 CFR 211.166(a)). 의약품 규격, 제조 또는 관리 절차의 변경 필요성을 판단하기 위해 각 의약품의 품질 기준을 최소 연 1회 평가할 수 있도록 하는 서면 기록의 유지(21 CFR 211.180(e)).

key_violations.description: 위 표시 기재 증거에 근거하면 (b)(4)는 (b)(4) 의약품으로 사용하도록 의도된 것이다. 따라서 이 의약품들은 표시 기재에서 처방·권장·제안된 사용 조건에서 일반적으로 안전하고 유효한 것으로 인정(GRASE)되지 않으므로 section 201(p) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(p) 에 따른 ‘신약(new drugs)’이다. 여기에 적용되지 않는 일부 예외를 제외하고, 신약은 section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355(a) 에 기술된 바와 같이 FDA의 승인 신청이 유효하지 않으면 주간 상거래(interstate commerce)에 도입되거나 도입을 위해 인도될 수 없다. 이 제품들에 대해 section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355 에 따른 승인 신청은 유효한 것이 없다. 따라서 이 제품들은 미승인 신약이다. 이러한 미승인 신약 제품을 주간 상거래에 도입하거나 도입을 위해 인도하는 것은 sections 301(d) and 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and 355(a) 를 위반한다.

QU 관련 회신(공급업체 평가·관리 절차 개정, 안정성 프로그램 마스터 플랜 갱신, 안정성 보고서·연간 제품 평가 소급 작성)도 시정 조치의 적절성·유효성을 검증할 근거 문서가 없고, 2020년 이후 안정성 시험 보고서 부재와 2024년 이후 (b)(4)개 제품의 연간 제품 평가 미완료 등 수년간 미검출된 시스템적 감독 실패를 다루지 않았다고 평가했다.

870193c29cc1.source_text: during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, Silgan Unicep Packaging, LLC, Facility Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3011913386, at 4122 South Grove Road, Spokane, Washington, from March 26 to April 2, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). In addition, violations were identified and documented during a review of the product labeling, including the product website at the internet address (b)(4) website in July 2026. Based on our review, “ (b)(4) ” are unapproved new drugs under section 505(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 355(a). As explained further below, introducing or delivering these products for introduction into interstate commerce is prohibited under sections 301(d) and 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and 355(a). We reviewed your April 22, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail and acknowledge receipt of your subsequent correspondence. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm contract manufactures non-sterile over-the-counter (OTC) (b)(4) drug products, including those labeled for use in (b)(4) . You failed to adequately investigate out-of-specification (OOS) microbiological testing results for components used to manufacture your drug products. For example, in November 2025, you obtained OOS microbiological results for (b)(4) lots (b)(4) . You prepared (b)(4) independent samples from each lot. You tested (b)(4) of the samples for total aerobic microbial count and the (b)(4) samples for total yeast and mold count. One sample from each lot exceeded your total yeast and mold count acceptance criterion of no more than (b)(4) colony forming units per gram. You did not perform an appropriate investigation into the OOS results. Rather, you invalidated the OOS results by averaging the (b)(4) total yeast and mold count sample results to obtain a passing result. You also revised your microbiological sampling plan to allow for averaging of test results for component testing. This practice is not in accordance with the United States Pharmacopeia <61> test method and is unacceptable as it obscures the detection of non-uniform microbiological contamination within a lot. You subsequently released (b)(4) lots and used them in the manufacture of (b)(4) Lot (b)(4) , distributed in (b)(4) . Notably, on (b)(4) , your customer, (b)(4) , initiated a Class I recall of (b)(4) lots of (b)(4) manufactured at your facility due to potential fungal contamination in your (b)(4) . The investigation associated with this recall is inadequate. For example, you implemented (b)(4) of incoming (b)(4) prior to filling to reduce bioburden, but subsequent OOS microbiological results obtained from (b)(4) lots demonstrate this corrective action was ineffective. Additionally, your change control associated with the (b)(4) process did not include ensuring appropriate validation of the process as well as evaluation of the (b)(4) . Further, you lacked cleaning procedures for the (b)(4) line, did not conduct cleaning validation of the (b)(4) line, and failed to include yeast and mold microbiological testing as part of your environmental monitoring program. Though your investigation into the potential fungal contamination documented an evaluation of the cleaning procedures and environmental monitoring, it did not identify nor appropriately follow-up on these risks related to potential mold contamination. In your response to the OOS microbiological test results, you state that you plan to update your work instructions to prohibit averaging of results. You commit to conducting a retrospective review of all drug product OOS events over a (b)(4) period to identify inadequate investigations and initiate customer notifications where warranted. You also commit to engaging a consultant for root cause analysis and failure investigation training, as well as updating the change control with a risk assessment of the (b)(4) . Your response is inadequate. You limit the retrospective review to documented OOS events and do not extend it to all microbiological test results to identify instances in which you inappropriately applied averaging to individual failing results to obtain overall passing results. This practice potentially resulted in the improper release of drug products. Furthermore, your response lacks an adequate plan to address product quality risks. It relies solely on procedural and documentation updates without an effectiveness verification plan and fails to address the systemic quality oversight failures that allowed these practices. Inadequate investigations can lead to unidentified root causes, ineffective corrective action and preventive action (CAPA), and recurring problems that compromise the ability to manufacture safe and effective drug products. For more information about handling OOS and failing test results, and documentation of your investigations, see FDA’s guidance document Investigating Out-of-Specification (OOS) Test Results for Pharmaceutical Production at https://www.fda.gov/media/158416/download. While this guidance addresses chemistry laboratory analyses, many of its principles are also relevant to investigating OOS microbiological results and out-of-trend results. In response to this letter, provide: A retrospective, independent review of all invalidated OOS (including in-process and release/stability testing) results for US products currently in the U.S. market and within expiry as of the date of this letter and a report summarizing the findings of the analysis, including the following for each OOS: o Determine whether the scientific justification and evidence relating to the invalidated OOS result conclusively or inconclusively demonstrates causative laboratory error. o For investigations that conclusively establish laboratory root cause, provide rationale and ensure that all other laboratory methods vulnerable to the same or similar root cause are identified for remediation. o For all OOS results found by the retrospective review to have an inconclusive or no root cause identified in the laboratory, include a thorough review of production (e.g., batch manufacturing records, adequacy of the manufacturing steps, suitability of equipment/facilities, variability of raw materials, process capability, deviation history, complaint history, batch failure history). Provide a summary of potential manufacturing root causes for each investigation, and any manufacturing operation improvements. A comprehensive review and remediation plan for your OOS and out-of-limit (OOL) result investigation systems. The CAPA should include but not be limited to addressing the following: o Quality unit (QU) oversight of laboratory investigations o Identification of adverse laboratory control trends o Resolution of causes of laboratory variation o Initiation of thorough investigations of potential manufacturing causes whenever a laboratory cause cannot be conclusively identified o Adequate scoping of each investigation and its CAPA o Revised OOS investigation procedures with these and other remediations o A similar review and remediation of your system for handling out-of-limit findings (i.e., data that falls outside action limits) A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, OOS results, OOL results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system. Your action plan should include, but not be limited to, significant improvements in investigation competencies, scope determination, root cause evaluation, CAPA effectiveness, quality unit oversight, and written procedures. Address how your firm will ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. o Furthermore, provide your (b)(4) validation study and updated cleaning procedures that demonstrate effectiveness in cleaning mold. Also provide the updated environmental monitoring study (WI-00480 Environmental Monitoring (Microbial) of Manufacturing and Laboratory Facilities Rev. 24) referenced in your response indicating sample locations, frequency, and duration, as well as alert and action limits. A comprehensive, independent assessment of the design and control of your firm’s manufacturing operations with a detailed and thorough review of all microbiological hazards. A detailed risk assessment addressing the hazards posed by distributing drug products with potentially objectionable contamination. Specify actions you will take in response to the risk assessment, such as customer notifications and product recalls. Complete investigations into all batches with potential objectionable microbial contamination or an OOS microbiological result whether or not later invalidated. The investigations should detail your findings regarding the root causes of the contamination. A summary of results from testing retain samples of all drug product batches within expiry. You should test microbiological quality (total counts and identification of bioburden to detect any objectionable microbes) of each batch. If testing yields an OOS result, indicate the corrective actions you will take, including notifying customers and initiating recalls. 2. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your QU failed to adequately oversee your OTC (b)(4) drug product manufacturing operations. For example, your QU failed to: Validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(2)). Follow a written testing program designed to assess the stability characteristics of drug products (21 CFR 211.166(a)). Maintain written records so that the quality standards of each drug product can be evaluated at least annually to determine the need for changes in drug product specifications, manufacturing, or control procedures (21 CFR 211.180(e)). In your response, you commit to revising your vendor evaluation and control procedure, updating your stability program master plan, and retrospectively generating stability study reports for all drug products. You also commit to updating your periodic product review procedure and completing retrospective annual product reviews for all manufactured drug products. Your response is inadequate. You did not provide supporting documentation to verify the adequacy and effectiveness of your corrective actions, nor did you address the systemic quality oversight failure that allowed deficiencies to persist undetected for multiple years, including the absence of stability study reports since 2020 and the failure to complete annual product reviews for (b)(4) of your drug products since 2024. Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accord with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your production and laboratory operations, we found your quality unit is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities. Executive management should immediately and comprehensively assess your company’s global manufacturing operations to ensure that your systems, processes, and products conform to FDA requirements. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. See FDA’s guidance documents ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System , at https://www.fda.gov/media/71553/download, and Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations , at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download, for help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to evaluate adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products Also describe how top management supports quality assurance and reliable operations, including but not limited to timely provision of resources to proactively address emerging manufacturing/quality issues and to assure a continuing state of control. Unapproved New Drug Violations Based on a review of the product labeling, “ (b)(4) ” are drugs under section 201(g)(1) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1), because they are intended for use in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease, and/or intended to affect the structure or any function of the body. Examples from product labeling, including the product website (b)(4) , that provide evidence of the intended uses (as defined in 21 CFR 201.128) of these products as a drug include, but may not be limited to, the following: (b)(4) Based on the above labeling evidence, (b)(4) intended for use as (b)(4) drug product. As such, these drug products are “new drugs” under section 201(p) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(p), because they are not generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE) for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in their labeling. With certain exceptions not applicable here, 1 a new drug may not be introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce without an approved application from FDA in effect, as described in section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355(a). No approved applications pursuant to section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355, are in effect for these products. Accordingly, these products are unapproved new drugs. The introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce of these unapproved new drug products violates sections 301(d) and 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and 355(a). Drug Recall On July 22, 2026, FDA held a teleconference with you, recommending that you recall drug products manufactured with (b)(4) lots (b)(4) currently in distribution from the U.S. market. On (b)(4) , your customer, (b)(4) , initiated a voluntary recall of (b)(4) lots (b)(4) currently distributed within the U.S. market. The recall was posted to the FDA’s Enforcement Report website at (b)(4) Drug Production Suspended We acknowledge your commitment to suspend production of all drugs at this facility. If you plan to resume any manufacturing operations regulated under the FD&C Act, notify this office before resuming your drug manufacturing operations. If you resume CGMP activities, you are responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure your firm is capable of ongoing CGMP compliance. In addition, based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of all corrective action and preventive action, before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. In your notification to the Agency, provide a summary of your remediations to demonstrate that you have appropriately completed all CAPA. Conclusion You are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. Unresolved violations may prevent other Federal agencies from awarding contracts. Failure to address violations may also cause FDA to withhold issuance of Export Certificates. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to address any violations. Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 3011913386 and ATTN: Renee A. Marcsisin, Ph.D. in the subject line of the email. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. key_violations.original: 1. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures that are designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile, and that include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes (21 CFR 211.113(b)). Poor Aseptic Practices and Cleanroom Behavior You manufacture sterile, (b)(4) drug products (including (b)(4) ). We observed poor aseptic practices during set-up and filling operations including, but not limited to: Operators repeatedly broke first air by reaching their arms, torsos, and heads over open sterile tubes, (b)(4) , and open (b)(4) during (b)(4) interventions. Operators used (b)(4) directly over open bottles, (b)(4) , and caps. An operator was observed working in the Grade A area of the (b)(4) line wearing a visibly stained gown.
key_violations.description: 1. 귀사는 무균으로 표방되는 의약품의 미생물 오염을 방지하도록 설계되고 모든 무균 공정 및 멸균 공정의 밸리데이션을 포함하는 적절한 서면 절차를 수립·준수하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.113(b)). 부적절한 무균 작업 및 청정실 행동: 귀사는 무균 (b)(4) 의약품((b)(4) 포함)을 제조한다. 당국은 셋업 및 충전 작업 중 다음을 포함하되 이에 국한되지 않는 부적절한 무균 작업을 관찰했다: 작업자들이 (b)(4) 개입(interventions) 중 개방된 무균 튜브, (b)(4), 개방된 (b)(4) 위로 팔·상체·머리를 뻗어 반복적으로 퍼스트 에어(first air)를 차단했다. 작업자들이 개방된 병, (b)(4), 캡 바로 위에서 (b)(4)를 사용했다. 한 작업자가 눈에 띄게 얼룩진 가운을 입은 채 (b)(4) 라인의 Grade A 구역에서 작업하는 것이 관찰되었다.
key_violations.risk: Grade A 구역에서 퍼스트 에어 차단과 오염된 가운 착용이 반복되어 노출된 무균 제품·용기에 직접적인 미생물 오염 위험이 있다.

key_violations.original: Inadequate Smoke Studies Dynamic airflow visualization (smoke) studies demonstrated that airflow patterns failed to adequately protect the aseptic processing line, including exposed sterile product and product contact equipment, from significant contamination hazards. For example, your dynamic smoke studies did not demonstrate unidirectional airflow protection of the production line when barrier (b)(4) were open. The studies showed air moving at a sharp angle upward toward return vents, leaving critical areas of your aseptic processing lines unprotected throughout the period in which the (b)(4) are opened. This fundamental design flaw enables the entrainment of lower-quality air from the surrounding lower-classified (Class 10,000/ISO 7) cleanroom into the Class 100 (ISO 5) aseptic processing line, posing a severe risk to product sterility.
key_violations.description: 부적절한 스모크 스터디: 동적 기류 시각화(스모크) 스터디 결과, 기류 패턴이 노출된 무균 제품과 제품 접촉 설비를 포함한 무균 공정 라인을 중대한 오염 위해로부터 적절히 보호하지 못하는 것으로 나타났다. 예를 들어 귀사의 동적 스모크 스터디는 차단막(barrier) (b)(4)가 열렸을 때 생산 라인의 일방향 기류(unidirectional airflow) 보호를 입증하지 못했다. 스터디에서는 공기가 리턴 벤트를 향해 급격한 각도로 상승하여, (b)(4)가 열려 있는 기간 내내 무균 공정 라인의 핵심 구역이 보호되지 않은 채 남는 것으로 나타났다. 이러한 근본적인 설계 결함은 주변의 하위 등급(Class 10,000/ISO 7) 청정실의 저품질 공기가 Class 100(ISO 5) 무균 공정 라인으로 유입(entrainment)되게 하여, 제품 무균성에 심각한 리스크를 초래한다.
key_violations.risk: barrier 개방 시 ISO 7 공기가 ISO 5 라인으로 유입되는 설계 결함으로, 해당 라인에서 생산된 전 배치의 무균성 보증이 불가능하다.

key_violations.original: Inadequate Equipment Cleaning and Sterilization Your aseptic processing operation is inadequately designed to prevent contamination of your sterile (b)(4) drug products. For example, you did not appropriately sterilize critical container-closure contact surfaces, such as the (b)(4) , bowl, track and (b)(4) equipment, as well as the (b)(4) , bowl, track, and (b)(4) equipment. Instead, you wipe these surfaces with sporicidal disinfectants. To ensure sterility, it is imperative that only sterilized equipment comes into direct contact with the sterile formulation, containers, and closures.
key_violations.description: 부적절한 설비 세척 및 멸균: 귀사의 무균 공정 운영은 무균 (b)(4) 의약품의 오염을 방지하도록 적절히 설계되어 있지 않다. 예를 들어 귀사는 (b)(4), 보울(bowl), 트랙 및 (b)(4) 설비와 (b)(4), 보울, 트랙 및 (b)(4) 설비 등 용기·마개와 직접 접촉하는 핵심 표면을 적절히 멸균하지 않았다. 대신 귀사는 이러한 표면을 포자사멸 소독제(sporicidal disinfectants)로 닦는다. 무균성을 보장하려면 멸균된 설비만이 무균 제제, 용기 및 마개와 직접 접촉하도록 하는 것이 필수적이다.
key_violations.risk: 용기·마개 접촉 표면을 멸균 대신 소독제 닦기로만 관리해, 멸균된 용기·마개가 충전 직전 비멸균 표면에 노출된다.

key_violations.original: 3. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your firm failed to establish an adequate QU with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacture of drug products. For example, you failed to ensure: Adherence to a stability program that supports the drug products’ expiration dating (21 CFR 211.166(a)). Contemporaneous documentation of EM and personnel monitoring sampling data in laboratory records (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
key_violations.description: 3. 귀사 품질 조직은 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity), 함량(strength), 품질(quality), 순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22). 귀사는 의약품 제조를 감독할 책임과 권한을 갖춘 적절한 QU를 수립하지 않았다. 예를 들어 귀사는 다음을 보장하지 않았다: 의약품의 유효기간 설정을 뒷받침하는 안정성 프로그램의 준수(21 CFR 211.166(a)). 실험실 기록에 환경 모니터링(EM) 및 작업자 모니터링 검체 채취 데이터의 동시적(contemporaneous) 기록(21 CFR 211.194(a)).
key_violations.risk: EM·작업자 모니터링 데이터의 비동시적 기록으로 무균 환경 관리 기록의 신뢰성이 훼손되고, 안정성 근거 없는 유효기간이 부여된다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 2026년 5월 15일자 Form FDA 483 회신과 후속 서신을 검토했다. 무균 작업 관련해 귀사는 (b)(4) 충전 라인을 평가·재설계하고 재설계 라인에서 스모크 스터디를 수행하며, 교육·자격인정을 통해 무균 작업자 행동을 개선하겠다고 했고, FDA는 (b)(4) 용액 라인 재설계와 (b)(4) 용액 라인 폐기 결정을 인지했다. 그러나 FDA는 회신이 상업 생산 중 작업자 관행을 효과적으로 모니터링하는 포괄적 프로그램을 갖추지 못했고(과거 실사에서도 부적절한 무균 행동이 지적되어 특히 우려됨), 기류 시각화 프로그램 개선 계획과 품질보증 감독 강화 및 자격 있는 전문가의 객관적 기류 일방향성 평가 방안이 부족하다고 평가했다. 설비 세척·EM·육안검사 관련 회신(라인 설계 개선, 세척·소독 절차 개정, EM 리스크 평가 및 성능 적격성 평가, 불량 분류·허용기준 설정)도 견고한 무균 공정 운영과 의미 있는 데이터 수집의 필요성을 체계적으로 다루지 않았고, 향후 멸균 가능한 설비 사용 보장 방안, 중요 활동 위치에서의 충분한 빈도의 EM 수행 방안, 개선된 육안검사 프로그램의 세부 내용이 없다고 지적했다. 또한 이전 경고서한(WL 320-19-01)에서 유사한 CGMP 위반이 지적되었음에도 반복된 것은 경영진의 감독과 통제가 불충분함을 보여준다고 평가했다.

items: 무균 작업·청정실 행동·서면 절차 준수를 보장하는 체계적 계획(소급 검토 및 전향적 관찰, 생산 관리 감독, QU 감독 빈도·깊이, 절차 및 작업 인체공학 평가와 CAPA 포함)과, 동적 조건에서의 독립적 기류 일방향성 평가(스모크 스터디)를 제출한다.
무균 공정·설비·시설의 모든 오염 위해에 대한 독립 리스크 평가와, 일정이 포함된 개선 계획(무균 공정 라인·청정실 설계 변경, 적격성 평가 및 밸리데이션 계획 포함)을 제출한다.
세척·소독·멸균 프로그램에 대한 소급 평가 기반 CAPA와, 결함 등급(critical·major·minor) 정의 및 개별 한도, 검사 시스템 적격성 평가를 포함한 육안검사 프로그램 독립 평가·개선 계획을 제출한다.
ALCOA 기록 보장을 위한 문서화 시스템 평가·CAPA와 QU 권한·독립성·자원 보장 계획을 제출하고, 21 CFR 211.34 에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트의 6대 시스템 감사와 CAPA 완료·유효성 평가를 받는다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 귀사는 미국 시장용 (b)(4) 의약품 생산 중단과 기타 (b)(4) 용액 생산 중지를 약속했으며, 생산 재개 전 당국에 통지해야 한다. 위반을 해결하지 않으면 section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act 에 따라 귀사 제조품의 미국 수입이 거부될 수 있고, CGMP 미준수로 불량의약품으로 보이는 물품은 억류되거나 수입 거부될 수 있다. 위반이 완전히 해소될 때까지 귀사를 제조소로 기재한 신규 신청·보완 신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있고 재실사가 이루어질 수 있다. 이전 경고서한(WL 320-19-01)에 이은 반복 위반이라는 점에서 규제 리스크가 가중된다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 무균으로 표방되는(purporting to be sterile) 의약품의 미생물 오염(microbiological contamination)을 방지하도록 설계되고, 모든 무균 공정 및 멸균 공정의 밸리데이션(validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes)을 포함하는 적절한 서면 절차(written procedures)를 수립·준수하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.113(b)).

귀사는 오염 또는 혼동(contamination or mix-ups)을 방지하는 데 필요한 별도 또는 구획된 구역(separate or defined areas) 또는 그 밖의 관리 시스템을 갖추지 않았으며 (21 CFR 211.42(c)), 공정 중 물질(in-process material)과 의약품의 특성에 변동을 일으킬 수 있는 제조 공정의 산출물을 모니터링하고 그 성능을 밸리데이션(validate)하기 위한 적절한 관리 절차(control procedures)를 수립·준수하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.110(a)).
귀사 품질 조직(quality unit)은 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity), 함량(strength), 품질(quality), 순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격(established specifications)을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.22).

8a404f9eaaf8.source_text: during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, Hanlim Pharm Co., Ltd., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3004886113, at 2-27 Yeongmun-ro, Yonginsi Ceoin-gu, Gyeonggi-do, from April 16 to April 24, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). We reviewed your May 15, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail and acknowledge receipt of your subsequent correspondence. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures that are designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile, and that include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes (21 CFR 211.113(b)). Poor Aseptic Practices and Cleanroom Behavior You manufacture sterile, (b)(4) drug products (including (b)(4) ). We observed poor aseptic practices during set-up and filling operations including, but not limited to: Operators repeatedly broke first air by reaching their arms, torsos, and heads over open sterile tubes, (b)(4) , and open (b)(4) during (b)(4) interventions. Operators used (b)(4) directly over open bottles, (b)(4) , and caps. An operator was observed working in the Grade A area of the (b)(4) line wearing a visibly stained gown. Inadequate Smoke Studies Dynamic airflow visualization (smoke) studies demonstrated that airflow patterns failed to adequately protect the aseptic processing line, including exposed sterile product and product contact equipment, from significant contamination hazards. For example, your dynamic smoke studies did not demonstrate unidirectional airflow protection of the production line when barrier (b)(4) were open. The studies showed air moving at a sharp angle upward toward return vents, leaving critical areas of your aseptic processing lines unprotected throughout the period in which the (b)(4) are opened. This fundamental design flaw enables the entrainment of lower-quality air from the surrounding lower-classified (Class 10,000/ISO 7) cleanroom into the Class 100 (ISO 5) aseptic processing line, posing a severe risk to product sterility. We also observed other design flaws in your production equipment that led to poor ergonomics and deficient aseptic practices that compromised unidirectional airflow. In addition, smoke studies were incomplete, as they failed to sufficiently evaluate airflow directionality during critical aseptic processing activities. In your response, you state you will assess and redesign your (b)(4) filling line (b)(4) to address deficiencies noted by FDA, and you will perform smoke studies on the newly redesigned line. Additionally, you state you will conduct extensive classroom and hands-on training, along with qualification to improve aseptic operator behavior. We acknowledge your commitment to redesigning the (b)(4) solution line, and your decision to decommission your (b)(4) solution lines. Your response is inadequate. It lacks a comprehensive program to effectively monitor personnel practices during commercial production, which is especially concerning given our past inspectional findings of poor aseptic behavior. Further, your response failed to provide sufficient plans to improve your airflow visualization program. Notably, your response lacked adequate provisions to improve quality assurance oversight, and ensure thorough and objective evaluation of future airflow unidirectionality studies by qualified subject matter experts. Your aseptic manufacturing processes should be designed, and operations executed, to prevent contamination hazards to your sterile product. Flaws in the design of cleanrooms and aseptic processing lines, or improper execution of aseptic operations can promote influx of contamination into the critical processing area. In response to this letter, provide: Your systematic plan to assure adherence to appropriate aseptic practices, cleanroom behavior, and written procedures, including but not limited to an independent assessment of the following with accompanying corrective action and preventive action (CAPA): o Suitability of actual practices based on extensive retrospective review and prospective observation of aseptic processing operations. o Deficiencies in production management oversight, and identification of specific improvements to ensure effective and routine supervisory oversight for all batches. o Frequency and depth of quality unit (QU) oversight (e.g., audit, ad hoc, daily interactions) of aseptic processing and its support operations. o Adequacy of written procedures and operational ergonomics. o The assessment should also evaluate how poor aseptic technique and cleanroom behavior may have affected the quality and sterility of your drugs. An independent, comprehensive evaluation of airflow unidirectionality in your aseptic processing operations. Ensure smoke studies are conducted under dynamic conditions with thorough and complete evaluations of aseptic processing line airflow unidirectionality, including the impact of aseptic interventions and dynamic interactions with the surrounding cleanroom. Conduct these smoke studies after you remediate your aseptic operation and using proper practices (e.g., neutrally buoyant media) to appropriately visualize airflow. 2. Your firm failed to have separate or defined areas or such other control systems necessary to prevent contamination or mix-ups (21 CFR 211.42(c)), and your firm failed to establish and follow adequate control procedures to monitor the output and to validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product (21 CFR 211.110(a)). Inadequate Equipment Cleaning and Sterilization Your aseptic processing operation is inadequately designed to prevent contamination of your sterile (b)(4) drug products. For example, you did not appropriately sterilize critical container-closure contact surfaces, such as the (b)(4) , bowl, track and (b)(4) equipment, as well as the (b)(4) , bowl, track, and (b)(4) equipment. Instead, you wipe these surfaces with sporicidal disinfectants. To ensure sterility, it is imperative that only sterilized equipment comes into direct contact with the sterile formulation, containers, and closures. Inadequate Environmental Monitoring You also failed to ensure adequate environmental monitoring (EM) of classified areas used for aseptic production of sterile (b)(4) drug products. The EM program used to monitor critical areas was deficient. You failed to demonstrate that the locations and frequencies established for viable air sampling, surface monitoring, and non-viable particulate sampling were adequately justified and sufficient to promptly detect contamination risks. For example, sampling was not adequate to evaluate the environment in proximity to containers and closures, nor on the surfaces of barriers facing your ISO 5 (Grade A) spaces. Because you had not established a sufficient EM program, you lacked evidence of daily environmental control that is foundational to assuring sterility of aseptically processed products. A vigilant, ongoing personnel and environmental monitoring program is essential to detect and respond to potential product contamination hazards in your manufacturing environment in a timely manner. Loss of environmental control in an aseptic manufacturing facility can ultimately pose a serious hazard to patients. Inadequate Visual Inspection Program Your visual inspection program for sterile (b)(4) drug products was deficient. Your firm failed to routinely categorize defects as part of your visual inspection program. In addition, you did not establish appropriate acceptance criteria. Notably, your process has experienced significant defect rates. It is important that visible particulate contamination is appropriately evaluated. When categorizing visible particles, extrinsic or foreign matter should receive special attention, as it may indicate possible insanitary or microbial contamination. Sterile manufacturing operations should be designed to prevent foreign contaminants, and such contamination should trigger a thorough investigation and appropriate CAPA. In your response, you state you will assess your (b)(4) filling line and improve its design. You state you will also revise cleaning and disinfection procedures, and conduct an EM risk assessment and subsequent EM performance qualification. Additionally, your response commits to improvements in visual inspection equipment, with better categorization of rejects and established acceptance criteria. Your response is inadequate. It fails to systematically address the need for robust aseptic processing operations and collection of more meaningful data to support aseptic operational control. It also lacks details describing how you will ensure use of sterilizable equipment in the future and conduct EM with sufficient frequency at locations where significant activity or exposure occurs during aseptic production. Additionally, you failed to provide the details of your improved visual inspection program, including how you will ensure thorough investigations, when appropriate. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent risk assessment of all contamination hazards with respect to your aseptic processes, equipment, and facilities, including but not limited to: o All human interactions within the ISO 5 area (e.g., risk reduction or elimination of (b)(4) interventions wherever possible) o Equipment suitability (e.g., reliability, capability, ergonomics, placement) and sufficient cleanroom space o Air quality in the ISO 5 area and surrounding room including, but not limited to, air volume and flow o Facility layout o Personnel Flow and Material Flow (movement throughout all rooms used to conduct and support sterile operations, and all material transfers) o Disinfection practices and procedures o Specific CAPA recommendations that will comprehensively address the design and control hazards identified in the risk assessment A detailed remediation plan with timelines to address the findings of the contamination hazards risk assessment. Describe specific tangible improvements to be made to aseptic processing operation design and control at your facility and explain how this CAPA plan will robustly remediate your deficient sterile manufacturing operations. Include comprehensive changes to the design of (b)(4) your aseptic processing lines and cleanrooms. Also, describe your plans for qualification and validation of your extensively remediated operations. A CAPA plan, based on the retrospective assessment of your cleaning and disinfection program, that includes appropriate remediations to your cleaning and disinfection processes and practices, and timelines for completion. Include the following as part of the assessment and CAPA plan: o A detailed summary of vulnerabilities in your process for lifecycle management of equipment cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization o A list of improvements, with an explanation how each will enhance cleaning and disinfection effectiveness o Improved ongoing verification of proper cleaning and disinfection execution o And, any other needed remediations A comprehensive, independent assessment and remediation plan for your drug product visual inspection program to ensure compliance with CGMP. The assessment and remediation should include, but not be limited to, the following: o Implement enhancements to your 100% visible particulate inspection practices, including defining critical, major, and minor defects and establish associated individual defect limits. o Ensure adequate methods, equipment, and personnel qualifications to reproducibly detect visible particulates, include particulates which historically have been found in your operation. o Conduct rigorous qualification studies to ensure your (b)(4) visible particulate inspection systems consistently and reproducibly detect the variety of visible particulates encountered in your drug products. o For drug products that are difficult to inspect (e.g., (b)(4) containers), implement destructive testing and other advanced technologies (e.g., (b)(4) ) as appropriate, with statistically significant sample sizes to test for defects. o Incorporate product-specific knowledge, process experience, deviation investigation analysis, complaint data, recall data, and quality risk management to improve the visual inspection program. o Associated remediations to your visual inspection program, including newly established written procedures, equipment, and methods. Include a summary of the review and recommendations made by your independent consultant. 3. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your firm failed to establish an adequate QU with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacture of drug products. For example, you failed to ensure: Adherence to a stability program that supports the drug products’ expiration dating (21 CFR 211.166(a)). Contemporaneous documentation of EM and personnel monitoring sampling data in laboratory records (21 CFR 211.194(a)). In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed CAPA plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous (ALCOA) records throughout your operation. A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority, independence, and resources to effectively function that includes, but is not limited to: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for independent QU oversight throughout your operations to ensure satisfactory procedures and adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products o Also, describe how executive management will support robust quality assurance at your firm, including but not limited to timely provision of resources that enable proactive detection and resolution of emerging manufacturing/quality issues to assure a continuing state of control Ineffective Quality System Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accord with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your production and laboratory operations, we found your QU is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities. Executive management should immediately and comprehensively assess your company’s global manufacturing operations to ensure that your systems, processes, and products conform to FDA requirements. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. For guidance on establishing and maintaining CGMP-compliant quality systems, see FDA guidances: Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development at https://www.fda.gov/media/71535/download, Q9(R1) Quality Risk Management at https://www.fda.gov/media/167721/download and Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System at https://www.fda.gov/media/71553/download. Drug Production Ceased and Suspended We acknowledge your commitment to suspend production of (b)(4) Drugs at this facility for the U.S. market and to cease production of all other (b)(4) solutions. If you plan to resume any manufacturing operations regulated under the FD&C Act, notify this office before resuming your drug manufacturing operations. If you resume CGMP activities, you are responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure your firm is capable of ongoing CGMP compliance. In addition, based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit 1 of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of all CAPA, before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance. In your notification to the Agency, provide a summary of your remediations to demonstrate that you have appropriately completed all CAPA. Repeats Violation at Facility In a previous warning letter (WL 320-19-01), FDA cited similar CGMP violations. You proposed specific remediations for these violations in your response. Repeated failures demonstrate that executive management oversight and control over the manufacture of drugs is inadequate. Additional Guidance on Aseptic Processing See FDA’s guidance document Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing—Current Good Manufacturing Practice to help you meet the CGMP requirements when manufacturing sterile drugs using aseptic processing at https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download. Conclusion You are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to any violations. Failure to address any violations may also result in the FDA refusing admission of articles manufactured at Hanlim Pharm Co., Ltd. at 2-27 Yeongmun-ro, Yonginsi Ceoin-gu, Gyeonggi-do into the United States under section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). Articles under this authority that appear to be adulterated may be detained or refused admission, in that the methods and controls used in their manufacture do not appear to conform to CGMP within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of this letter 2 . Identify your written response with FEI 3004886113 and ATTN: Compliance officer Philip Kreiter in the letter. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration cc: Registered U.S. Agent Toscano Consulting Group, Inc (b)(4) _____________________ 1 i.e. Quality System, Facilities & Equipment System, Materials System, Production System, Packaging & Labeling System, and Laboratory Control System per FDA’s guidance document Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations. 2 Under program enhancements for the Generic Drug User Fee Amendments (GDUFA) reauthorization for fiscal years (FYs) 2023-2027, also known as the GDUFA III Commitment Letter, your facility may be eligible for a Post-Warning Letter Meeting to obtain preliminary feedback from FDA on the adequacy and completeness of your corrective action plans.
